# package sparkplugb

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-sparkplugb"
```

Package sparkplugb holds what the edge, host and app packages of this Sparkplug B module share: the Logger and FieldLogger they log through and the RetryPolicy, such as ExponentialBackoff, that decides reconnection.

## Types

### type ExponentialBackoff

```go
type ExponentialBackoff struct {
	// Initial is the delay after the first failure; 500 ms when zero.
	Initial time.Duration
	// Max caps the delay; 30 s when zero.
	Max time.Duration
	// Attempts is the number of retries; 5 when zero, unbounded when
	// negative.
	Attempts int
	// NoJitter waits the delay itself, for tests.
	NoJitter bool
}
```

ExponentialBackoff is the RetryPolicy that retries after a delay that doubles from Initial up to Max, with jitter: the wait is drawn at random between half of the delay and the delay, so that devices that failed together do not come back together.

The zero value retries up to 5 times from 500 ms (Attempts 5, Initial 500 ms, Max 30 s).

#### func (ExponentialBackoff) Delay

```go
func (b ExponentialBackoff) Delay(attempt int) time.Duration
```

Delay returns the wait after the failure of attempt, regardless of the error and of Attempts.

#### func (ExponentialBackoff) ShouldRetry

```go
func (b ExponentialBackoff) ShouldRetry(attempt int, err error) (bool, time.Duration)
```

ShouldRetry implements RetryPolicy.

### type FieldLogger

```go
type FieldLogger interface {
	Logger
	With(kv ...any) FieldLogger
}
```

FieldLogger is a Logger that keeps fields (key-value pairs) with its lines: With returns one that adds kv to every line. The packages of this module name themselves (component=edge, ...) through it when a Logger is one.

#### func NewSlogLogger

```go
func NewSlogLogger(h slog.Handler) FieldLogger
```

NewSlogLogger returns a FieldLogger that writes to the slog handler h, at the slog levels of the same names.

#### func NewStdLogger

```go
func NewStdLogger(l *log.Logger, debug bool) FieldLogger
```

NewStdLogger returns a Logger that writes to l (the standard logger when nil), with the level in front of each line, from Info up; NewStdLogger with debug true writes Debug lines too.

### type HeldDropMetrics

```go
type HeldDropMetrics interface {
	OnHeldDrop(groupID, edgeNodeID, messageType string)
}
```

HeldDropMetrics is implemented by the Metrics of a host or application that counts the messages it drops from those it holds for reordering. The held messages are bounded over all edge nodes, at 4096 messages and 8 MiB of payload (SECURITY.md); to make room for the next one, the oldest held message of any edge node is dropped. OnHeldDrop is called for each message so dropped, with its edge node and message type (NDATA, DDATA, DBIRTH or DDEATH), with none of the runtime's locks held. A held message that waited longer than 30 s for the gap before it is dropped without this call.

### type Logger

```go
type Logger interface {
	Debugf(format string, args ...any)
	Infof(format string, args ...any)
	Warnf(format string, args ...any)
	Errorf(format string, args ...any)
}
```

Logger receives the log of the edge nodes, host applications and applications of this module: set it as the Logger of their configuration. A nil Logger logs nothing. Debug is the detail of every publish and subscribe; Info, what changes (a state transition, a rebirth); Warn, what failed and is retried; Error, what fails a call or stops work.

A Logger is called from many goroutines, and must not block.

#### func ComponentLogger

```go
func ComponentLogger(l Logger, name string) Logger
```

ComponentLogger returns the Logger a package of this module uses for l: NopLogger for nil, and for a FieldLogger one with component=name.

#### func NopLogger

```go
func NopLogger() Logger
```

NopLogger returns a Logger that logs nothing.

### type RetryPolicy

```go
type RetryPolicy interface {
	ShouldRetry(attempt int, err error) (retry bool, wait time.Duration)
}
```

RetryPolicy decides whether a failed connection or publish is made again, and when: the edge nodes, host applications and applications of this module take one for their reconnection. attempt is the number of the attempt that failed, from 0. A policy is called from many goroutines.

#### func NoRetry

```go
func NoRetry() RetryPolicy
```

NoRetry returns a RetryPolicy that never retries.

### type SessionChecks

```go
type SessionChecks uint8
```

SessionChecks selects stricter checks that a host application (package host) or an application (package app) makes on the data messages of an edge node around its NBIRTH, to drop a message of the session that ended instead of applying it to the new one. The zero value makes none: that is the default, and what Sparkplug B 3.0 asks for.

Sparkplug carries no session in NDATA and DDATA, and MQTT orders messages per topic only, so a broker may deliver a message of the ending session among those of the new one (go-sparkplugb#24, LIMITATIONS.md). Without these checks two such messages are applied to the new session; each check drops one of them, at the cost of dropping valid messages of edge nodes that do not meet its assumption. A dropped message of the new session leaves a gap in its sequence, and the gap costs a rebirth. Births and deaths are never dropped by these checks.

Use them only for edge nodes whose payload timestamp is the time of publishing, from a clock that does not go back, and that stamp no birth before the NBIRTH it follows, as this module's edge package does. host.Config and app.Config take them for every edge node (SessionChecks) or per edge node (SessionChecksFor).

```go
const (
	// CheckBirthMillisecond drops an NDATA or DDATA that arrived before the
	// NBIRTH of its edge node and is stamped in the millisecond of that
	// NBIRTH, or was applied before it with that timestamp. By default it is
	// taken for the new session's: births and the data right after them share
	// a millisecond. With this check, a new-session NDATA or DDATA stamped in
	// the NBIRTH's millisecond that the broker delivers before the NBIRTH is
	// dropped.
	CheckBirthMillisecond SessionChecks = 1 << iota

	// CheckOlderInSequence drops an NDATA or DDATA that carries the sequence
	// number the session expects next but is stamped before the session's
	// NBIRTH, within 30 s of that NBIRTH. By default a message in sequence is
	// applied whatever its timestamp. With this check, data of an edge node
	// that stamps a payload earlier than its time of publishing (the time a
	// value was sampled, say) or whose clock goes back is dropped after each
	// NBIRTH.
	CheckOlderInSequence

	// SessionChecksAll is every check.
	SessionChecksAll = CheckBirthMillisecond | CheckOlderInSequence
)
```

### type SessionDropMetrics

```go
type SessionDropMetrics interface {
	OnSessionDrop(groupID, edgeNodeID, messageType string)
}
```

SessionDropMetrics is implemented by the Metrics of a host or application that counts the data messages and births it drops as belonging to a session that has ended: those published before the current NBIRTH and out of sequence, which are always dropped, and those the SessionChecks drop. OnSessionDrop is called with the edge node and the message type (NDATA, DDATA, DBIRTH or DDEATH), with none of the runtime's locks held.
